claims.text: A two-stage heat treatment will induce fine, coherent intermetallic precipitates in an initially single-phase Ti–Ni high-entropy alloy.
The precipitate-forming heat treatment will improve elevated-temperature mechanical properties relative to the untreated single-phase material.
A high-temperature solutionizing step will homogenize the alloy structure.
Aging at approximately 700 °C for about 1 hour will induce nanoscale, coherent precipitation of a secondary intermetallic phase.
The induced coherent intermetallic precipitates will be uniformly distributed throughout the matrix.
The coherent precipitates will pin dislocations.
The coherent precipitates will stabilize the microstructure during high-temperature exposure.
Dislocation pinning and microstructural stabilization will reduce creep and delay softening.
Reduced creep and delayed softening will improve high-temperature yield strength and overall mechanical stability.
The aged alloy will have higher high-temperature yield strength than the untreated as-cast or as-quenched alloy.
The aged alloy will have a lower creep rate than the untreated as-cast or as-quenched alloy.
The expected mechanical-property improvement will be significant, although its magnitude is unknown.
The hypothesis is applicable at test temperatures of approximately 600–800 °C.
The hypothesis is limited to initially single-phase Ti–Ni high-entropy alloys in which Ti and Ni are dominant and significant secondary elemental additions are absent.
